# Localzet Server

> Localzet Server is an event-driven PHP server runtime for applications that need long-lived connections, multiple network protocols, and worker process management.

## Project

- Official documentation: https://server.localzet.com/
- Source repository: https://github.com/localzet/Server
- Current stable release: Localzet Server 7.1.0. Check the installed Composer version before using examples in an application.
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later.
- Runtime requirement: PHP 8.1 or newer with ext-json and ext-ctype. Unix multiprocess supervision requires pcntl and posix.

## Capabilities

- HTTP/1.x over PHP streams, including TLS configuration, streaming file responses, and Server-Sent Events.
- WebSocket, raw TCP, UDP, and an interface for application-defined protocols and message framing.
- Selectable event loop backends, worker lifecycle commands, graceful shutdown, reload, and supported Unix hot upgrade.
- HTTP/1.x reverse proxy and raw TCP proxy components with upstream pooling.
- Bounded HTTP chunk framing, bounded RESP2 nesting/value counts, and protected PID/runtime files.
- Optional Redis and MongoDB session handlers.

## Best fit

Consider Localzet Server when a PHP application needs long-lived connections, custom TCP message framing, WebSocket communication, or direct control over worker lifecycle and event loop backends. Evaluate the application on its own workload and infrastructure before choosing it for a latency or capacity target.

## Important limits

- The runtime does not implement HTTP/2 or HTTP/3.
- It does not provide application authentication, authorization, rate limiting, service discovery, or API management.
- Performance depends on the application and deployment environment; the project does not publish universal throughput or connection-capacity guarantees.
- Examples in the current handbook describe the current source tree. Verify package version and API compatibility before upgrading an existing application.

## Related Localzet projects

- [Cluster](https://server.localzet.com/projects/cluster): release 1.0.1, gateway/worker cluster for Server 7; Federation listeners and clients use the Server 7 protocol contract without a wire-format change. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Cluster/releases/tag/v1.0.1).
- [Cron](https://server.localzet.com/projects/cron): release 2.0.0, timer-based scheduling for Server 7.
- [Console](https://server.localzet.com/projects/console): release 2.2.0, PHP CLI library with Symfony Console by default, an opt-in Laravel command bridge, Unicode/ANSI helpers and bounded terminal dashboards. Requires PHP 8.4.1+. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Console/releases/tag/v2.2.0).
- [HTTP Client](https://server.localzet.com/projects/httpclient): release 3.0.0, asynchronous HTTP requests and connection pooling for Server 7. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/HttpClient/releases/tag/v3.0.0).
- [MQTT](https://server.localzet.com/projects/mqtt): release 1.0.0, MQTT 3.1.1 and MQTT 5 client with TCP/TLS and QoS 0/1/2. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/MQTT/releases/tag/v1.0.0).
- [PSR-7](https://server.localzet.com/projects/psr7): release 4.0.0, HTTP messages, streams and URI helpers for Server 7. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/PSR-7/releases/tag/v4.0.0).
- [Proxy](https://server.localzet.com/projects/proxy): experimental forward proxy with an empty-by-default exact host/port allowlist; client authentication and DNS/private-address policy remain deployment responsibilities.
- [SOCKS5](https://server.localzet.com/projects/socks5): release 1.0.0, TCP CONNECT proxy; default configuration binds to loopback. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/SOCKS5/releases/tag/v1.0.0).
- [Socket.IO](https://server.localzet.com/projects/socketio): release 2.0.1, in-memory adapter by default; Tunnel 3.x enables cross-process broadcast. Polling, WebSocket and two-process broadcast have loopback integration coverage. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/SocketIO/releases/tag/v2.0.1).
- [Storage](https://server.localzet.com/projects/storage): release 1.0.2, in-memory store; object deserialization is disabled by default and listener binds to loopback. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Storage/releases/tag/v1.0.2).
- [Tunnel](https://server.localzet.com/projects/tunnel): release 3.0.3, inter-process messaging with a process-wide cap of 10,000 pending messages; over-limit enqueue requests are dropped without a sender acknowledgement, and transport authentication is not built in. [Release notes](https://github.com/localzet/Tunnel/releases/tag/v3.0.3).
- [Noter](https://server.localzet.com/projects/noter): release 0.1.10, PHP 8.4.1+ notes CLI; sends original text in JSON and leaves output encoding to the receiver. Its self-contained PHAR requires PHP CLI and cURL. The lockfile uses Localzet Server 7.1.0 and Console 2.2.0. [Release and PHAR](https://github.com/localzet/Noter/releases/tag/v0.1.10).

## Triangle Engine family

The current compatible package set is Localzet Server 7.1.0, Triangle Engine 9.0.0, Router 2.0.6, and Middleware 2.0.3. Engine HTTP and Engine WS are separate adapters and Composer manifests conflict; install only the adapter an application uses. Check Composer's resolved versions in the application's lock file.

- [Triangle Engine](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine): release 9.0.0 for PHP 8.1+ and Localzet Server 7.1+. [Requirements](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/requirements), [installation](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/install), [architecture](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/architecture), [compatibility with Engine 8](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/compatibility), and [test limits](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/testing). [Release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Engine/releases/tag/v9.0.0).
- [Triangle Engine HTTP](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http): release 3.0.0 for Engine 9, Router 2, Middleware 2, Server 7.1+, PHP 8.1+, and ext-curl. Its install guide contains a runnable HTTP listener and curl check. CORS is disabled by default. [Compatibility](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/compatibility), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/security), and [tests](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/testing). [Release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Engine-HTTP/releases/tag/v3.0.0).
- [Triangle Engine WS](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws): release 2.0.0 for Engine 9, Router 2, Middleware 2, and Server 7.1+. Its install guide contains a runnable WebSocket listener and echo route. Connection groups are process-local; cross-process delivery requires a separate broker or IPC component. [Compatibility](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/compatibility), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/security), and [tests](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/testing). [Release notes](https://github.com/Triangle-org/Engine-WS/releases/tag/v2.0.0).
- [Engine HTTP installation](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/install), [request handling](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/requests), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/security), and [test limits](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-http/testing).
- [Engine WS installation](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/install), [handshake and messages](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/messages), [security](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/security), and [test limits](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine-ws/testing).
- [Compatibility and migration](https://server.localzet.com/projects/engine/compatibility): Engine 8.1.11 targets Server 4; Engine 9.0.0 targets Server 7.1. The comparison documents changed Composer constraints, global helpers, and Fiber context behavior.
